text: Nobody tells you a condom company plans to grow revenue one hundred and twenty three percent in one year.
Meet Cupid. It makes male and female condoms, lubricants and medical test kits. And now perfumes, deodorants and face wash too.
It has two businesses. Global tenders and exports brought in two hundred and eight crore last year. Sales in India, one hundred and twenty two crore.

How do tenders work? Governments and the United Nations buy condoms in bulk, from approved makers only. Cupid was the first in the world approved by W. H. O. and U. N. F. P. A. for both male and female condoms.

That opened big doors. A five year South Africa tender, to supply up to all of the country's needs. Brazil, six point two five million female condoms. And exports to over one hundred and twenty five countries.
Now the growth. Revenue was three hundred and fifty eight crore in FY26. The company guides above eight hundred crore for FY27, and targets fifteen hundred crore by FY29.
The first quarter already showed it. Revenue up one hundred and forty two percent, profit up one hundred and ninety three percent.

To deliver, it is building a new plant at Palava, for one point two five billion male condoms a year. Plus a factory plan in South Africa, and shelf space in over two hundred and eighty retail stores.
The stock? About seven times its fifty two week low. Market value, forty six thousand crore.
But check the price. That is about one hundred and eighty four times the profit it hopes to make this year. Guidance is not results, and tenders can be lumpy.
Save this, and follow for more. Would you add Cupid to your watchlist? Yes or no?
